items.title: IMO and ICAO SAR Experts Finalize Updates To International Search And Rescue Manual
points: The ICAO/IMO Joint Working Group on Harmonization of Aeronautical and Maritime Search and Rescue has finalized updates to the International Aeronautical and Maritime Search and Rescue Manual (IAMSAR).
The IAMSAR Manual provides international guidelines for a common aeronautical and maritime approach to organizing search and rescue (SAR) services.
It includes three volumes: Volume I on Organization and Management; Volume II on Mission Coordination; and Volume III on Mobile Facilities, which are updated approximately every three years.
During its thirty-third meeting held in Malmö, Sweden (9-13 November), the Joint Working Group finalized draft amendments to all three volumes of the IAMSAR Manual for its 2028 edition.
These amendments will be submitted for endorsement by the IMO’s Sub-Committee on Navigation, Communications and Search and Rescue (NCSR), with a view to adoption by the Maritime Safety Committee.
The 33rd meeting of the ICAO/IMO Joint Working Group was co-organized by the IMO and ICAO Secretariats and supported by the Swedish Transport Agency and the Swedish Maritime Administration.

items.title: India needs a comprehensive doctrine on space security
points: Communications, navigation, weather forecasting, disaster management, agriculture, banking, logistics and critical infrastructure are increasingly dependent on satellites and space-enabled services.
In India, space capabilities support the armed forces through communications, positioning, surveillance, timing and situational awareness.
Space is therefore no longer a separate technological sector but an essential component of national resilience and strategic autonomy.
As dependence expands, disruption can have consequences for markets, governance, security and society at large.
The character of threats in space is changing.
Space systems can now be affected by jamming and spoofing that interfere with communications and navigation.
The vulnerability lies not only in the satellite itself, but in the wider architecture connecting space assets to users on Earth.
This shift from destruction to disruption has made space security a more complex challenge for states.

items.title: All-too fallible: On India’s vote against moratorium on death penalty
points: At the same time, the Supreme Court has increasingly restricted capital punishment and research has failed to find evidence of additional deterrence over life imprisonment.
India’s distinction between judicial executions and extrajudicial killings is legally valid but its further claim that due process protects people facing execution is less so.
The country had 574 people on death row on December 31, 2025, the highest since 2016, thanks to trial court rulings, challenging claims about judicial safeguards in practice.
The report of the 2015 Law Commission headed by Justice A.P.
Shah said the death penalty “fails to achieve any constitutionally valid penological goals” and recommended abolishing it for all crimes except terrorism and waging war.

items.title: Gulf Oil Flow at Risk From Lack of Empty Tankers, Tracker Says
points: By Alaric Nightingale (Bloomberg) — The number of empty tankers sailing to collect cargoes of Middle East crude is sliding, a trend that could jeopardize the recent revival in the region’s oil flows to global markets, according to Tankertrackers.com, a…
The industry uses two main ship types to get oil from the Persian Gulf to the world: very large crude carriers, which transport 2 million-barrel cargoes, and Suezmaxes that move about half that.
The collective capacity of those vessels sailing empty to the region has declined by about 40% since the end of August, according to Tankertrackers.com figures.
While the market is intensely focused on how much oil leaves the Middle East, those flows are only possible if there’s a steady stream of ships arriving to pick up the barrels.

The Iran war has meant that some vessels refuse to go through the Strait of Hormuz, instead receiving cargoes in locations like the Gulf of Oman from tankers that are willing to risk shuttling through the crucial waterway.

points: SEBI reduces initial margin requirements for agriculture and non-agriculture commodity derivatives trading, with revised rates effective December 1, 2026. | Photo Credit: ABEER KHAN The capital market regulator SEBI has reduced the margin requirement for…

items.title: Don't Blame Punjab Farmers For Pollution, Says Union Agriculture Minister
points: Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has come out in support of Punjab's farmers amid criticism over stubble burning and its contribution to Delhi's air pollution.
During his visit to Samrala in Ludhiana, Chouhan inspected stubble management practices in fields and praised the state's farmers, saying they were being unnecessarily blamed for pollution.

Congratulating farmers for what he described as a historic reduction in farm fire incidents, the Union Minister said Punjab's farmers had demonstrated that paddy stubble could be effectively managed without burning it.
Punjab recorded 461 fresh stubble-burning incidents on November 16, taking the total number of farm fires since September 15 to 6,433.
Ferozepur has emerged as the biggest hotspot with 847 incidents, followed by Sangrur at 741, Tarn Taran at 705, Bathinda at 591 and Patiala at 416.
Environmental compensation of nearly Rs 1.13 crore has been imposed on violators, of which Rs 40.60 lakh has been recovered.
